title: Events are the Wrong Abstraction for Your AI Agents - Mason Egger, Temporal.io
talk_summary: A Temporal vendor talk arguing that event-driven architectures put the wrong abstraction at the center of agent systems, causing scattered logic, ad hoc state machines, race conditions, and fragile coupling at design time. It pitches durable execution (crash-proof, state-preserving, retry-built-in workflows) as the fix, with events hidden under the hood.

takeaways.technique: Durable execution for long agent runs
takeaways.what_they_do: Persist every function call's inputs/outputs/returns automatically so a crashed run resumes from the last good checkpoint instead of restarting, with retries built into each call.
takeaways.evidence_quote: durable execution will basically take that state that it saved, restart the execution and resume execution from the point of the last known good last known save point

takeaways.technique: Retries as a platform primitive, not agent logic
takeaways.what_they_do: Wrap LLM/tool calls in automatic retry-until-success so agents don't spend context or reasoning on rate limits and transient failures.
takeaways.evidence_quote: If the LLM goes down, we're getting rate limit automatic retries. You don't even have to develop that.

takeaways.technique: Keep business logic at the center, minimize glue
takeaways.what_they_do: Argue that most of an EDA diagram is failure-handling scaffolding, not core logic; reorient so the workflow is the primary artifact and plumbing is hidden.
takeaways.evidence_quote: there are more parts about handling the events than there was the core logic of the actual application

takeaways.technique: Explicit state machines over implicit event chains
takeaways.what_they_do: Warn that event-driven services become ad hoc state machines with local caches and no transactions, producing race conditions and hard-to-trace bugs.
takeaways.evidence_quote: every single one of our services is now an ad hoc state machine

takeaways.what_they_do: Build reliability into software (checkpointed, resumable execution) rather than into hardware, so runs survive machine/process loss.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's builds reliability into the software side, not the hardware side
